title: Prophetic Patterns and Repair
editor: Working editorial assessments developed with AI assistance for Micah Blumberg; open to author revision.
scope: Ranked textual and conduct comparisons, not probabilities of supernatural identity. This is a selected, incomplete research edition. A low score may reflect limited research; consult coverage and the actual cases. The authorial theology is not presented as the consensus of the compared traditions.

criteria.name: Personal supremacy
criteria.observation: The vision joins extraordinary authority with boasting and public awe.
criteria.pattern: Compare indispensability, immunity from correction and exaltation of personal power.
criteria.narrative: Require the specified blasphemous claims; strong leadership rhetoric alone is incomplete.

criteria.name: Allegiance above accountability
criteria.pattern: Compare institutional demands for personal allegiance that displace independent judgment.
criteria.narrative: An oath or political endorsement is not, without more evidence, worship of the beast.

criteria.name: Violence and persecution
criteria.observation: War against the saints and captivity are part of the account.
criteria.pattern: Compare coercive domination and persecution while naming victims and agents.
criteria.narrative: Generic interstate war is not automatically the specified war against saints.

criteria.name: Sacred authority used to shield power
criteria.observation: Blasphemous speech concerns God and the divine dwelling.
criteria.pattern: Ask whether sacred claims exempt power from the moral standard it invokes.
criteria.narrative: Specify actual speech against God; using a religious quotation is not sufficient.

criteria.name: Extent of governing power
criteria.observation: Authority extends across peoples, languages and nations.
criteria.pattern: Measure documented breadth of institutional power, not fame alone.
criteria.narrative: National power or influence is not authority over every nation.

criteria.name: Healed mortal wound
criteria.observation: A head appears mortally wounded and the wound is healed.
criteria.pattern: Historical comeback analogies require an explicit argument, not assumed resurrection.
criteria.narrative: The kind of wound, healing, sword reference and resulting allegiance must be addressed.

criteria.name: Forty-two months
criteria.observation: The vision specifies a 42-month period of authority.
criteria.pattern: A recurring moral pattern does not require an invented start date.
criteria.narrative: Provide independently grounded endpoints and count convention; no moving dates.

criteria.name: Name and number
criteria.observation: The number is associated with the beast's name.
criteria.pattern: Reception-history evidence, not a measure of someone's harmful conduct.
criteria.narrative: Predeclare language, spelling and calculation; test alternatives and textual variants.

criteria.name: Promotes another authority
criteria.observation: The second beast directs worship toward the first.
criteria.pattern: Document who legitimizes whom, through which public action, and why the dependence matters.
criteria.narrative: Political support alone does not establish worship or all the delegated authority.

criteria.name: Benign appearance and contrary operation
criteria.observation: Lamb-like horns contrast with dragon-like speech.
criteria.pattern: Compare professed care or truth with documented contradictory conduct.
criteria.narrative: Neither a religious identity nor an AI product label proves deception.

criteria.name: Signs that persuade
criteria.observation: Signs include fire from heaven and deception.
criteria.pattern: Specify how a display transfers allegiance; technical impressiveness alone earns no match.
criteria.narrative: Require the narrated sign and deception, not merely rockets or impressive software.

criteria.name: Speaking image and compelled allegiance
criteria.observation: An image is made, speaks and is associated with lethal coercion.
criteria.pattern: Separate representation, voice, the represented ruler and coercive function.
criteria.narrative: A chatbot or avatar alone does not supply the specified image, worship and killing.

criteria.name: Conditional economic access
criteria.observation: Buying and selling depend on the mark, name or number.
criteria.pattern: Compare material dependence and exclusion linked to the dominant authority.
criteria.narrative: Procurement restrictions are not universal commerce restrictions or the bodily mark.

criteria.name: Material care
criteria.observation: The passage identifies feeding, welcome and care as consequential conduct.
criteria.pattern: Look for delivered assistance, beneficiaries and continuing obligations.
criteria.narrative: Claims of benevolence do not establish delivery; seek independent outcome records.

criteria.name: Protection and justice
criteria.observation: Religious performance is judged beside wrongdoing and defense of vulnerable people.
criteria.pattern: Evaluate protection of those exposed to harm, including politically inconvenient victims.
criteria.narrative: An announcement alone is not achieved justice or full compliance with the passage.

criteria.name: Peace without retaliatory cruelty
criteria.observation: Peacemaking and enemy-love constrain responses to hostility.
criteria.pattern: Examine protective resistance, restraint and repair without demanding submission to abuse.
criteria.narrative: A declaration of peace does not prove a durable settlement or love of enemies.

criteria.name: The same standard for oneself
criteria.observation: Self-examination and discernment by fruits appear within one chapter.
criteria.pattern: Ask whether accurate criticism changes conduct rather than becoming evidence of disloyalty.
criteria.narrative: Calling oneself righteous is not evidence that the standard actually corrects one.

profiles.name: First Beast correspondence
profiles.note: A selected Revelation 13 rubric. Pattern and narrative-specific readings are separate scoring lenses.

profiles.name: Second Beast correspondence

profiles.name: Christlike repair by works
profiles.note: A positive conduct comparison open to every person. It is neither the inverse of a Beast score nor a certification as Messiah.

bridges.connection: Test authority by works and inspect domination rather than merely professed identity.
bridges.difference: Matthew's warning about judging others also applies to the evaluator. Revelation's first and second actors remain distinct.

bridges.connection: Generational potentiality permits examining readiness and later accomplishment separately.
bridges.difference: Davidic lineage, Torah and specified achievements are not replaced with popularity or nationality. Zelenskyy's case is the author's proposal, not a designation by these sources.

bridges.connection: Distinct prophetic and messianic functions support comparing roles rather than demanding one undifferentiated office.
bridges.difference: A prophet and messiahs of Aaron and Israel do not amount to a messiah for every present-day nation.

bridges.passage: Gospel of Philip, living resurrection passage
bridges.connection: Transformation during life supplies a connection to inward formation and the recipient of a teaching.
bridges.difference: This passage does not define every Gnostic school or erase external catastrophe.

bridges.connection: Restoration and the return of legitimate teaching can be compared with other renewal traditions.
bridges.difference: The community account retains Moses' exceptional status and rejects other faiths' prophets; respectful comparison must not erase this disagreement.

bridges.connection: Difference in laws and paths is set beside competition in good works: a concrete opening for an ethical bridge.
bridges.difference: The verse also asserts Quranic authority. It does not equate the Messiah, Mahdi, Dajjal and Revelation's beasts. Those require distinct Sunni and Shia source dossiers.

bridges.connection: Authority loses legitimacy through unrighteous domination; persuasion and love offer a constructive alternative.
bridges.difference: The passage concerns priesthood. Extending it to governments or AI companies is the present comparative interpretation.

bridges.passage: Birur and tikun in Moshe Miller's exposition
bridges.connection: The work of distinguishing and restoring sparks supplies a comparison with repairing distorted patterns and relations.
bridges.difference: A contemporary comparative use does not turn ritual cosmology into a measured physical process or claim identity with SAN or SIT.

bridges.connection: Cyrus demonstrates that a named anointed role can be examined in its specific textual function.
bridges.difference: This is not evidence that every beneficial ruler fulfills later messianic expectations.

tasks.title: Publish inspectable rankings
tasks.acceptance: A public figure's rank resolves to selected criteria, scores, counterweights and sources. No unknown cell is silently counted as a known non-match.

tasks.title: Separate lenses and record dependencies
tasks.acceptance: Narrative-specific and recurring readings use separate inputs; duplicate assessments for one person/criterion are rejected.

tasks.title: Restore the prior reception register
tasks.acceptance: All 22 attributed claims and 26 source records remain inspectable, with Netanyahu's identity correction displayed in the current roster.

tasks.title: Develop the interfaith repair charter
tasks.acceptance: State the author's metaphysical starting point, compare specific texts, and preserve substantive disagreement.

tasks.title: Complete the current-figure evidence dossiers
tasks.acceptance: For each requested figure recover at least three independently checked dated actions, unfavorable and favorable countercases, and named counterpart relations.

tasks.title: Audit historical reception and missed predictions
tasks.acceptance: Recover original Napoleon, Reagan and other claims; preserve failed and revised expectations, spelling choices and publication dates.

tasks.title: Collate Qumran and Gnostic passage units
tasks.acceptance: Use named critical editions; distinguish copy dates, composition, narrated events and present interpretation.

tasks.title: Extend Jewish, Samaritan, Muslim and LDS dossiers
tasks.acceptance: Compare tradition-specific messianic qualifications and restoration; consult primary Muslim texts and separate Sunni/Shia differences.

tasks.title: Investigate the Exodus and computational-God bridges
tasks.acceptance: Keep physical disaster, textual memory, divine-name history, agency argument and authorial theology as explicit linked hypotheses with their own evidence.

tasks.title: Calibrate reviewer disagreement and selection bias
tasks.acceptance: Two independent reviewers score the same blinded cases; record disagreements, counterexamples and rank sensitivity without treating agreement as truth.

tasks.title: Join the research to the book and museum
tasks.acceptance: Extend existing chapter arguments with completed dossiers; regenerate changed narration rather than relabeling prior recordings.

tasks.title: Audit outcomes and changes through time
tasks.acceptance: Version complete assessments with event and review dates; add independently assessed outcomes to the existing forecast ledger without moving original goalposts.
